scope: instrument calibration only, not flame/FDS calibration

partition.method: chronological holdout: latest ceil(20% of observed days); all sessions and restrictors on a day stay together

quality_issues.action: retain raw points but exclude from model fitting and evaluation

extraction.source_note: Note:  Data is organized by number of restrictors used.  Not all restrictors were comonly used, so often the fan calibration only includes the restrictors of interest for that day. Some days we ran out of time before the fan cal could be complete.   There are additional flow values that were used during testing when the fan is on at a fixed voltage for at least a few minutes.   Note that the fan turns off at a finite voltage (above 3.8 volts), so it is recommended to not use the 3.8 volts zero flow value.
extraction.measurement_location_note: Based on SPICE fan calibration data at 56 mm downstream, 36 mm from bottom (centerline)

limitations: Published velocities are estimates derived from a display conversion, not independent velocity measurements.
No uncertainty for the factor or the underlying flow instrument is provided in this workbook.
Fan shutdown occurs above 3.8 V; the explicit 3.8 V zero anchors are excluded per source warning.
Soot cleaning and device state alter the calibration. A global cross-day curve is not a universal calibration.
Per-session interpolation must not extrapolate or transfer to another apparatus or cabin inlet.
The first session DATE and GMT disagree and is not used to fit or evaluate the models.
Multiple controls during a burn cannot be collapsed into one mean airflow or treated as independent experiments.
